extracted.intended_audience: public information officers (PIOs), joint information center (JIC) staff, emergency managers, EOC personnel, and public affairs personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for operating the Joint Information System (JIS) including the roles and responsibilities of the Public Information Officer (PIO) and the Joint Information Center (JIC) during incidents and EOC activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIS components: PIO and JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Information Officer (PIO) and Joint Information Center (JIC) are two supporting elements of the JIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and recognize both elements as core components of JIS operations; use this structure when planning public information activities during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO as a key member of ICS and EOC organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Information Officer (PIO) is a key member of ICS and EOC organizations, though they might go by a different title in EOCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a designated PIO (or equivalent titled role) is integrated into the Incident Command System and EOC staffing and decision-making structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advising leadership on public information matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Advising the Incident Commander, Unified Command or EOC director on public information matters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO should provide counsel to incident leadership on messaging strategy, public information priorities, and coordination with partners and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating accurate, accessible, and timely information
rubrics_metrics.description: Gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating accurate, accessible, and timely information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO must establish processes to collect facts, confirm accuracy, coordinate messaging across agencies, and release information in formats and channels accessible to affected audiences and the media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling inquiries from media, public and elected officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling inquiries from the media, public and elected officials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain mechanisms and staffing for receiving and responding to inquiries promptly and consistently; coordinate answers to ensure unified messaging and appropriate information disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing emergency public information and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing emergency public information and warnings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver clear, actionable warnings and protective-action messages during emergencies as part of the PIO's core responsibilities; prioritize speed and clarity while ensuring accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting rumor monitoring and response
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement rumor monitoring processes to detect misinformation and deliver corrective messaging quickly to maintain public trust and reduce confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC as the central location for JIS operations and public affairs functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC is a central location that houses JIS operations and where public information staff perform essential information and public affairs functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stand up a physical or virtual JIC to centralize public information activities, co-locate public affairs staff where possible, and support coordinated information production and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC quantity: normally single but flexible to multiple JICs
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, an incident should have a single JIC, but the JIS is flexible and can accommodate multiple JICs if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a single JIC for unity of effort; plan for and coordinate multiple JICs only when incident scale, geography, or organizational complexity necessitates them, ensuring inter-JIC coordination mechanisms are in place.
